# Makepad

Makepad apps (Fab, for CAD and 3D printing, and more) are compiled from source on this computer
by the Makepad Runner. Your coding agent can install one, start it and use its tools from the
shell. No plugin or MCP server is needed.

## Install and start an app

macOS (Apple silicon) and Linux (x86_64, glibc):

    curl -fsSL https://makepad.nl/runner/unix | sh -s -- open fab

Windows (from cmd, PowerShell or a POSIX shell):

    powershell -NoProfile -c "& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://makepad.nl/runner/windows.ps1))) open fab"

The first start downloads Rust, builds the loader and compiles the app for this computer: many
minutes. A window on the screen shows how far it is. Run the line with a long timeout, or in the
background, and read its output. If your shell stops waiting, run the same line again: it
continues where it is. Later starts reuse what was built.

It ends with a block like this one:

    Ready: fab pid=48213 makepad=/home/you/makepad-runner/makepad
    Fab is running. Talk to it from your shell:
      /home/you/makepad-runner/makepad inspect 48213 tools                       (its AI tools)
      /home/you/makepad-runner/makepad inspect 48213 call <service>.<tool> {..}  (one tool call; pictures are saved as files)
      /home/you/makepad-runner/makepad inspect 48213 grab                        (a picture of its window)
      /home/you/makepad-runner/makepad inspect 48213 help                        (every remote command)

On Windows the makepad path ends in makepad.cmd. When the app cannot be found by its pid, the
block names its socket path instead; use whatever the block prints.

## Talk to the running app

Use the makepad path and the target (pid or socket) from the ready block:

    <makepad> inspect <target> tools               the app's AI tools, with their arguments
    <makepad> inspect <target> call fab.render {}  call one tool; pictures are written to files, their paths printed
    <makepad> inspect <target> grab                a picture of the app's window
    <makepad> inspect <target> help                every remote command

To start the app again later, or to find it when it already runs:

    <makepad> open fab
